designSummary: Quantitative strand: descriptive completion estimates and a longitudinal model of weekly completion; qualitative strand: reflexive thematic analysis; integration by joint display.
sampleSize: All eligible patients are included, about 420. For an overall completion near 60 percent, 420 patients give a 95 percent confidence interval of about plus or minus 4.7 percentage points (square root of 0.24 over 420, times 1.96). About 420 patients over 12 weeks give about 5,000 patient-weeks, which supports a model of weekly completion with five pre-specified terms. The interview sample of 20 to 24 patients and 10 to 12 nurses is set by information power: a focused aim, purposive sampling across age, deprivation and language, and an analysis of patterns already found in the data.
primaryAnalysis: Proportion of expected reports completed over weeks 1 to 12 with 95 percent confidence intervals, by clinic, age group (under 75, 75 or over) and deprivation quintile. Mechanism: mixed-effects logistic regression of weekly completion on an unanswered severe alert in the previous week, adjusted for the severity score of the previous report, age group, deprivation quintile and treatment week, with a random intercept for patient.
secondaryAnalysis: Median time to nurse contact after alerts, weekday against weekend; emergency visits and unplanned admissions described by completion tertile without causal inference; interview themes coded with COM-B and set against the quantitative patterns in a joint display.
missingData: A missing report is the outcome, not missing data; patients who die or stop chemotherapy leave the denominator at that week; missing alert contact times are reported and treated as unanswered only in a sensitivity analysis.
multiplicity: One primary estimate and one pre-specified mechanism model; subgroup estimates are descriptive.
software: R (lme4) for the quantitative strand; NVivo for coding; the joint display in a shared spreadsheet.
overfittingGuards: Five model terms fixed before exports are examined
Subgroups limited to age, deprivation and clinic
summary: About 420 patients give a completion estimate within about 4.7 points; about 5,000 patient-weeks support the mechanism model; interviews sized by information power.
